_channel_note: MUST be sdk for P5. The ahk channel is a machine-wide singleton keyed on claude_window_title, so a concurrent run on that channel would prove nothing about the thing P5 exists to test.
_lanes_note: Machine-wide cap on concurrent executor calls across ALL callers (RC + Sibling-A), enforced via C:/ProgramData/lw-loop/slots. Both repos MUST agree on this number.
_ignore_no_progress_note: true on purpose: the P5 scope is one appended line per cycle, and the same-sha guard is not what is under test here.
cycle_command: P5 CONCURRENT-RUN SMOKE, Tier-0 docs only, RC repo. Read ops/loop/control/cycle.txt for cycle number N. Append EXACTLY ONE line to docs/_archive/2026-07-26-p5-concurrent-smoke.md (create with a one-line heading if absent), of the form: "- RC cycle N: <one sentence on what you observed> (head <8-char sha before your commit>)". STRICT SCOPE: touch NO other file, and NEVER any path under C:/Sibling-A. No code changes. 7-bit ASCII only, no em-dashes or smart quotes. Then git add that one file, commit with a conventional-commit subject, push to origin main.
_cycle_command_note: cycle_command, NOT fixed_directive. fixed_directive skips BOTH the director and the auditor, so no gemini call ever happens and P5 condition 4 (gemini windows never overlap) would pass VACUOUSLY by doing nothing. cycle_command skips only the director and KEEPS the auditor, so every cycle makes a real gemini call through GEMINI_MUTEX - which is the thing condition 4 measures.
_cycle_budget_note: REMOVED 2026-07-26 (operator): no --max-budget-usd on the sdk channel. The Claude Code Max 20x plan is a SUBSCRIPTION - the CLI's total_cost_usd is a notional API-equivalent price, not money being billed, so a dollar cap truncates a cycle on a number that does not correspond to actual spend. The gate run read $22.01 of a $25 cap and would have been cut off by a slightly larger scope, for no real saving. UPDATED 2026-08-01: ceiling_usd is GONE too - it railed the metered vendor, and with that vendor retired the only spend left was Claude's, so leaving the check would have inverted it into a cap on exactly the spend policy says must never be capped. executor_usd is still recorded per cycle as a workload-size signal - read it as relative effort, never as spend.
_adjudicator_vendor_note: CLAUDE-ONLY since 2026-08-01 (operator). The loop self-adjudicates: the same vendor executes, directs and audits a cycle, and the read-only guarantee is --permission-mode plan, not vendor diversity. The second vendor and ALL of its machinery are DELETED, not merely unselected - backend registry, exhaustion-signature matching, the sticky failover and the spend ceiling are gone from ops/loop/adjudicator.py. There is therefore NO one-key rollback any more; restoring a second vendor means restoring the code, and the reasons not to are in docs/CONCURRENT_HEADLESS_CONTRACT.md section 9. An 'adjudicator' key naming anything but claude is ignored with a log line rather than honoured.
